ev.q: Approximately 16% of adults with COVID-like symptoms reported persistent symptoms 12 months after a positive or negative SARS-CoV-2 test result.
18.3% of COVID test–positive participants and 16.1% of COVID test–negative participants reported persistent symptoms of any type through 12 months
The prevalence of symptom persistence was defined as the proportion of participants with persistent symptoms at each time point
Binomial 95% CIs were calculated for each outcome within each group
Approximately one half of participants in each group experienced any symptom at 12 months.
Overall, no difference in symptom prevalence between COVID test–positive and COVID test–negative participant groups was observed
Symptom prevalence declined over time within each symptom category

methods_quotes.q: binomial 95% CIs were calculated for each outcome within each group and Pearson’s chi-square tests were used to test for differences in proportions
statistical comparisons of the COVID test–positive and COVID test–negative groups were performed using Pearson’s chi-square tests
a participant was defined as having a persistent symptom if he or she had the symptom at that visit and all previous periods
Pearson’s chi-square tests were used to test for differences in proportions at each time point
